messages:
Alex: FYI support ticket from Acme — overnight bulk embeddings job (~120k items) started getting 429s around 02:15 UTC. Also saw a dimension error in the app logs: "DimensionMismatch: expected 1024, got 768". Anyone seen this combo before?

Maria: Can you paste the exact error snippet, model name, and batch size? Also: does the client set embedding_dim explicitly or are they merging outputs from different models?

Alex: Error snippet:
```json
{"error":"DimensionMismatch","message":"expected 1024, got 768","model":"embed-large-v2","request_id":"req_9ab3"}
```
Batching: they send 256 items per POST from a batching proxy, and run ~40 concurrent workers. Auth looks fine. 429s show up intermittently — some responses include Retry-After, some don't.

Kevin: Probable two things: (1) proxy sometimes mixes embeddings from embed-base (768) with embed-large (1024) -> dimension mismatch; (2) throughput/burst limits -> 429. Immediate mitigation: reduce concurrency to <=8, batch size to 16-32, and add exponential backoff + jitter. Also add a pre-send dim validation step in the proxy.

Jamie (SRE): Agree with Kevin. On infra side I can see the project spiked the per-minute embedding unit quota at 02:14:52 -> internal ratelimiter tripped and returned 429s without Retry-After for ~90s due to windowing edge case. We're rolling a small patch to surface X-RateLimit-* and Retry-After consistently. Customer should still implement backoff with jitter.

Maria: Quick repro steps for our support run: 
- curl POST to /v1/embeddings with model=embed-large-v2 and a single wrong-dimension vector to reproduce the dimension error
- run repeated small batches (n=8) with high concurrency to trigger 429s
Example curl to test connectivity:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v2","input":["test string"]}'
```
Inspect response headers for X-Quota-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Limit and Retry-After.

Alex: Customer-side root cause: their batching proxy combined payloads from two internal pipelines (embed-base and embed-large) and sent mixed-dim vectors as one request. Proxy didn't tag per-item model id. They'll patch the proxy to bucket by model_id/dim and send separate requests per model. We'll recommend smaller batches on retry.

Kevin: I'll draft a short playbook to send to the customer. Key items: validate dims client-side, batch-by-model, reduce concurrency, and implement retry/backoff with jitter. Example backoff pattern: 
```python
import time, random
for attempt in range(6):
    resp = send_batch()
    if resp.status == 429:
        sleep = (2 ** attempt) + random.random()
        time.sleep(sleep)
        continue
    break
```

Support Bot: Ticket #SUP-4821 created and linked to this thread. Assigned to Kevin. Priority: P2. Customer notified.

Jamie (SRE): :thumbsup: I'll follow up on the header fix and apply a temporary burst uplift for the affected project. Ops will post ETA in the ticket.

Kevin: Action items recap:
- Support (Maria): run repro steps and send playbook to customer
- Customer: patch proxy to bucket by model id/dim and reduce concurrency/batch size
- SRE (Jamie): temporary burst uplift + header patch to include Retry-After/X-RateLimit headers
I'll update SUP-4821 after customer confirms changes.
